title: Signed tensor densities and diagram budgets for the Thorp shuffle
coverage:
I checked Part I (Sections 1, 2 and 3) line by line, since together they prove Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2.

Section 1:
- Thorp-to-sweep conjugation.
- Annihilation and finite-gap lemmas.
- Support lower bound.
- The near-row hook inequality.
- Degree sums.

Section 2:
- Signed super Schur–Weyl sector decomposition.
- Density domination of the type projection: Haar scalar at least e^{-F}/u.
- Carrier upper bound via highest weight plus AM-GM.
- One-sided angle theorem: support-inverse trick, commutation of T with P_K and P, the cell-wise z_ij column-sum identity, and the AM-GM step for Phi_K at most e^l. I also verified this theorem numerically for q=2 on a 2x2 grid over all types; the largest ratio of the norm to the bound was 0.083.
- Pointwise-stabilizer restriction lemma.
- Hook-dimension and multiplicity bounds.
- Local stabilizer trace, including the occurrence-transfer quantifier.

Section 3:
- Sparse estimate: inclusion-exclusion over A, vanishing at isolated labels, the two-trip row-sum bound, the joint-inclusion bound preserved under fair swaps, weighted neighbor sum at most 2dk/n, and the rooted plane-forest count.
- Order of choosing r and d_0.
- ALT reduction.
- Truncation to q = n^{1/64} parts (F-F' at least (L-l) log q against the Lipschitz constant of g).
- Labeled-hole multiplicity D_gamma and the w=z diagonal-block argument.
- Error budgets: carrier, partition and type counts are all O(n^{1-xi}).
- Pairing of child entropies with the angle bound, via -(1-eta')w + min(0, w-F) at most -(1-eta')F.
- Hole-placement sum via method of types (independent row and column histograms).
- D_lambda at most binom(n,l) e^F D_gamma.
- Absorption by the increments of eta_d and kappa_d (order d^{-1/2}).
- Zero-hole Durfee occurrence: hook factors checked, including the (1+y/a) per-cell bound.
- Fourier sum after 6r sweeps.

Not audited: Part II (Sections 3b through 10: alternative and refined bounds). The main result does not depend on it.
main_claim: Theorem 1.1: there is a fixed moment r such that, for every lambda ⊢ n = 2^d and every signed occurrence V_alpha ⊗ V_{beta^t} ⊗ V_gamma in Res V_lambda, log(D_lambda Tr (B_n^* B_n)^r) ≤ eta_d F(alpha,beta) + g_n(l). Corollary 1.2: a fixed number L of coordinate sweeps makes the L^2 distance of the full permutation density go to 0, so the Thorp shuffle mixes in t_mix = Theta(d) physical shuffles.
sibling_notes: This is the family-238 paper that holds the full every-occurrence induction. The three sibling entries already on the board (conditional information, partial-permutation Fourier, random coordinate frames) all report no_gap_found. Their isotypic and trimming tools look like Part II's Section 3b, which I did not audit. The O(d) mixing conclusion rests only on Part I.
